title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & tools
author: Ava Chen
summary: A single reference covering what it means to work at Redwood: our values and culture, role families and career ladders, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding process, and the core internal tools new hires need to be productive.
body:
Overview
-------
Redwood Inference is a developer-first, production-focused company. This handbook page summarizes the practical details every Redwooder should know about working here: our culture and values, how roles and career ladders work, key benefits and perks, an end-to-end hiring and onboarding overview, and the internal tools and access flows that enable day-to-day work.

Working at Redwood - Culture & expectations
----------------------------------------
- Mission-first: we prioritize ship-readiness, reliability, and measurable customer impact.
- Ownership: engineers and product teams are expected to own features from design through production.
- Data-informed decisions: we favor measurable experiments (e.g., benchmarks, perf tests, evals) over opinions.
- Inclusive collaboration: cross-functional teamwork is core - engineering, product, SRE, and customer success work closely.
- Remote-first with regional hubs: flexible remote work, with optional office hubs in key regions.

Roles and career ladders
-----------------------
This section describes role families, common leveling expectations, and promotion processes. Managers and ICs have separate ladders.

Role families covered (representative):
- Engineering (frontend, backend, infra, runtime, SRE)
- Product (product managers, product designers)
- Data & Applied ML (research engineers, eval engineers)
- Platform & Security (platform engineers, security engineers)
- Customer-facing (solutions engineering, customer success, support)
- Cross-functional (people-ops, finance, go-to-market)

Leveling overview (example expectations)
- L1 / Associate: learning role. Delivers well-scoped tasks with guidance.
- L2 / Mid: owns moderate-scope projects, contributes to design, and mentors interns.
- L3 / Senior: designs and leads cross-team projects, influences product and technical direction.
- L4 / Staff / Principal: leads critical initiatives, sets standards, and coaches across teams.
- L5 / Senior Principal / Distinguished: company-level technical or product leadership.

Promotion process (high level)
1. Prepare a promotion packet: impact examples, PRs, product outcomes, customer metrics, and peer feedback.
2. Manager review and calibration: manager collects feedback and proposes level change.
3. Calibration committee: cross-functional panel reviews packets, confirms expectations and equity with compensation partner.
4. Decision and timing: if approved, compensation and title changes are communicated; if deferred, manager provides concrete growth plan.

Typical promotion timeline: most promotions follow an 12-24 month rhythm dependent on demonstrated impact and readiness.

Career development resources
- Manager 1:1s and career conversations (documented goals)
- Learning budget: $2,000 USD/year (see Benefits section)
- Mentorship program: opt-in pairing with senior engineers or product leaders
- Internal trainings: quarterly bootcamps (onboarding, security, model-serving best practices)

Benefits & perks (practical details)
----------------------------------
Redwood offers a competitive benefits package. Below are the commonly used items and practical notes for enrollment. For complete plan documents see Benefits Portal (People Ops).

Health & financial benefits
- Medical, dental, vision: multiple plan options; Redwood covers a portion of premiums for employees and eligible dependents.
- 401(k) / retirement: company match up to the plan limits; enrollment window is 30 days after start date.
- Equity: option grants for full-time employees; vesting schedule is 4 years with 1-year cliff (standard).

Leave & time off
- Flexible PTO: no hard cap; team guidelines and manager approval required for planned long leaves.
- Parental leave: primary leave up to 18 weeks (paid); secondary/partner leave up to 8 weeks (paid).
- Caregiver and bereavement policies: see People Ops for details.

Compensation & financial support
- Competitive base + equity + bonus structure where applicable.
- Relocation assistance: offered case-by-case for hires relocating for a role.

Wellness & work environment perks
- Home office stipend: $500 one-time for remote hires + $50/month remote-work allowance.
- Learning & conference budget: $2,000 USD/year per employee for books, trainings, conferences.
- Mental health support: access to counseling services and an employee assistance program.
- Wellness days: 1 additional paid day per quarter for mental health/rest.

Commuting & hubs
- Regional hub benefits: cafe credits, travel stipend for adverse weather days, and team social budgets.

Hiring & onboarding overview
---------------------------
This section is a practical playbook for hiring managers, interviewers, and new hires.

Recruiting steps (standard process)
1. Requisition + hiring plan: manager opens req in Greenhouse with role profile and success metrics.
2. Screening: recruiter screens candidates, then schedules a hiring manager screen.
3. Interview loop: typically includes technical screen, onsite (virtual) loop with product and cross-functional interviews, and a hiring committee debrief.
4. Homework or take-home exercise: used sparingly and time-boxed (recommended max 4 hours).
5. Offer and negotiation: People Ops provides market data and final offer package.
6. Background check and references: initiated after verbal acceptance.

Interviewer guidelines (short)
- Use rubrics: assess against leveling rubric and take thorough notes.
- Reduce bias: follow structured interviews, avoid off-the-cuff judgments.
- Timely feedback: submit interviewer feedback within 48 hours.

New hire onboarding (first 90 days)
Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- Complete paperwork via People Ops portal (W-4, I-9 equivalents depending on country).
- Set up accounts: Okta SSO, Slack, GitHub, GCP/AWS console access (see Internal Tools section).

Day 1-7: orientation
- Orientation session run by People Ops: company values, benefits enrollment, and policies.
- Team welcome: manager completes team intro, sets first-week goals, and assigns onboarding buddy.

First 30 days:
- Complete role-specific training and read key docs (product roadmap, architecture overviews, runtime docs).
- Deliver a small onboarding project with mentor review.

30-90 days:
- Own a scoped feature or operational task.
- Schedule a 30/60/90 checkpoint with manager to review progress and calibrate goals.

Onboarding checklist (must-complete items)
- Accounts provisioned: Okta, Slack, GitHub, Confluence, Jira, CI/CD access
- Security training completed: secure-sdlc intro, phishing awareness
- Benefits enrollment window started
- Buddy meetings scheduled (weekly for first month)

Internal tools & access guide
---------------------------
Core systems and who owns access requests: 
- Okta (SSO) - owner: IT / People Ops. First step for access to most other tools.
- Slack - owner: Eng-DevEx for channel standards; create essential channels with naming conventions (#team-name, #oncall-<service>).
- Confluence - owner: Eng-DevEx; main knowledge base (this handbook lives under /company-handbook).
- GitHub (org) - owner: Eng-Platform; request team membership for repo access.
- Jira - owner: Eng-Platform; project roles assigned per team.
- Cloud console (GCP/AWS) - owner: Eng-Infra; service accounts created through infra tickets.
- CI/CD (Buildkite/GitHub Actions) - owner: Eng-Platform; request deploy permissions after code review training.
- Monitoring & alerting (Prometheus/Datadog) - owner: Eng-SRE; alert subscriptions managed in team dashboards.

Access request flow
1. Request Okta account via People Ops onboarding form (link in People Ops portal).
2. Once Okta is active, submit specific tool access requests through the Access Request form (Confluence link).
3. Team leads approve repository and cloud access; infra tickets are triaged with a 3-business-day SLA for standard requests.

Security & compliance responsibilities
- Complete mandatory security training in the first 14 days.
- Follow secure-SDLC guidelines for code reviews and secrets management.
- Use company-approved key management (KMS/HSM) for customer data encryption in Private deployments.

Who to contact (quick list)
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood-inference.com - benefits, onboarding paperwork, payroll questions.
- IT / Access: it-support@redwood-inference.com - Okta issues, laptop provisioning.
- Eng-Platform: eng-platform@redwood-inference.com - GitHub/Jira/CI questions.
- Eng-SRE: oncall@redwood-inference.com - monitoring and incident routing.

Frequently asked questions (short)
Q: How do I request a conference budget?
A: Submit a request through the learning budget form; manager approval required. Allow up to 2 weeks for review.

Q: Who approves flexible PTO?
A: Your manager approves planned time off; for extended leaves coordinate with People Ops.

Q: How long until equity vests?
A: Standard 4-year vesting with a 1-year cliff; consult People Ops for grant specifics.
